10	
11	# Summary
12	
13	The change shape is right — single `task_runs` queue with `ClaimNextRun` authoritative, no parallel queue or peer claimer, append-only migrations v44–v47, clean contract/codegen co-ship, full HTTP/UDS/CLI parity, `agh.runtime` as a first-class runtime peer, guidance-only response register, and preserved `claim_token` redaction — but three flagship behaviors are stubbed or wrong while every surface (contract, CLI, native tool, web, docs, skill) was completed to look done. Channel `fanout_policy`/`coordinator_peer_id` are stored and surfaced everywhere yet never consulted in routing; designated fan-out is non-functional for N≥2; digest "coalescing" is unimplemented (its config knobs are dead); mute drops directly-addressed traffic; and the entire subscription/mute/digest/activation delivery machinery ships with zero behavioral tests — which is exactly why the broken behaviors slipped through.
14	
15	# Blockers
16	
17	## B-001 — Channel `fanout_policy`/`coordinator_peer_id` are fully surfaced but never enforced in routing
18	
19	- File: internal/network/router.go
20	- Line: 1207
21	- Issue: The delivery-set computation `(*Router).deliveriesFromLocalPeers` (router.go:1207-1233) and `selectActivatedThreadPeers` (1234-1272) never read the channel's `fanout_policy` or `coordinator_peer_id`. For an unaddressed empty-participant thread they always run the same capability-ranked top-K activation regardless of the channel's policy. I confirmed first-hand: `grep -rni "fanout|coordinator_peer|capability_match|all_members" internal/network` (non-test) returns nothing. The field is persisted (network_channels, migration v44), validated (`store.ValidateNetworkFanoutPolicy`), settable via CLI (`agh network channels update`), native tool (`agh__network_channel_update`), HTTP+UDS PATCH, the web policy dialog, and documented in the site + bundled skill — but selecting `coordinator` or `all_members` has zero runtime effect, and `capability_match` runs unconditionally. This is the central A1 deliverable ("channel activation policy") and it is not wired into delivery.
22	- Rationale: This is a spec-completeness failure on the round's headline feature plus a Truthful-UI/Truthful-tool violation. CLAUDE.md: "Don't render controls or metrics the runtime doesn't actually support"; `internal/CLAUDE.md` agent-manageability requires control surfaces to actually control. Operators and agents set a policy that silently does nothing, and the web dialog (channel-policy-dialog.tsx:46-52,170) and docs (threads.mdx, channels-and-peers.mdx, delivery.mdx, skills/agh/references/network.md:84) assert `coordinator`/`all_members` routing behaviors that do not exist. Verified independently by me and by two review agents that each read router.go directly.
23	- Suggested fix: In `deliveriesFromLocalPeers`, resolve the channel entry (workspace_id, channel) and branch on `fanout_policy`: `coordinator` → full-inject the `coordinator_peer_id` (digest-fallback when missing/unavailable), `all_members` → full fan-out, `capability_match` (default) → the current activation with digest fallback (see B-004). Then correct the web/docs/skill copy in the same cut. If policy enforcement cannot land this round, do a truthful descope: remove/relabel the coordinator + all_members controls and doc claims rather than shipping controls that lie.
24	
25	## B-002 — Designated fan-out with N≥2 is non-functional (2nd sibling rejected at enqueue)
26	
27	- File: internal/store/globaldb/global_db_task_aux.go
28	- Line: 1477
29	- Issue: `enqueueFanOutTaskRuns` (api/core/tasks.go:1213-1240) loops `manager.EnqueueRun` once per designation. `EnqueueRun` → `ReserveQueuedRun` (global_db_task_aux.go:618) calls `findOpenRunIDForQueuedRunReservation` (1477-1504), which selects ANY run `WHERE task_id = ? AND status NOT IN (completed, failed, canceled)` with no `designation_group_id` awareness. The first designation creates a `queued` (non-terminal) run; the second designation's reservation finds that open run and returns `ErrInvalidStatusTransition` ("finish or cancel it before enqueueing another run"). So a fan-out of N≥2 aborts after creating exactly one run — the core C1 feature (N parallel sibling runs, default cap 5) never produces siblings. Per-designation idempotency keys differ, so the idempotency short-circuit does not save it.
30	- Rationale: Correctness bug that makes the flagship execution-plane deliverable non-functional. It went undetected because there is no test that enqueues 2+ designated runs through the real store/`ReserveQueuedRun` path — the observer test seeds sibling runs directly via `CreateTaskRun`, and the in-memory manager stub replicates the same designation-blind `hasOpenRun` guard (manager_test.go:1305). This is the single-durable-queue invariant reused with a single-open-run guard that fan-out contradicts.
31	- Suggested fix: Make the open-run guard designation-aware: when reserving a run whose `designation_group_id` is set, exclude runs sharing that same group id from the open-run check (siblings are expected to coexist as `queued`), while keeping the guard for non-designated enqueues. Apply the same fix to the in-memory test stub and add a store-level test that enqueues N=2..5 designated runs and asserts N distinct `queued` rows share one group id.
32	
33	## B-003 — Digest mode does not coalesce; `digest_flush_interval`/`digest_max_envelopes` are dead knobs; cost still charged per-envelope
34	
35	- File: internal/network/delivery.go
36	- Line: 1170
37	- Issue: `formatNetworkDigestMessage` (delivery.go:1170-1204) takes ONE `Envelope` and renders a compact preview-only wrapper. There is no batching loop and no flush timer; the delivery worker dequeues one item at a time (delivery.go ~595-651). The config keys `DigestFlushInterval` (250ms) and `DigestMaxEnvelopes` (10) are defined, defaulted, and validated (config.go:468-469,1745-1749) but never read in `internal/network` (confirmed: `grep DigestFlushInterval|DigestMaxEnvelopes internal --include=*.go` hits only config/merge/tool_surface/api-settings). Because there is no coalescing, prompt cost is still attributed per-envelope as a full injection (`recordThreadPeerPromptCost` with `DeliveredCount: 1`, manager.go ~1885) — the plan's explicit "allocate cost across included envelopes by canonical size" is not implemented.
38	- Rationale: Named A3 deliverable and Test Plan item ("digest coalescing, and honest cost allocation") unimplemented, with validated-but-dead config (a Truthful-config problem: settings UI and CLI accept knobs that do nothing). The web dialog (channel-policy-dialog.tsx:171), site docs (delivery-and-safety.mdx:41 and the `digest_max_envelopes` = "Maximum envelopes summarized into one digest prompt" row at :96; threads.mdx:73), and bundled skill (network.md:90) all claim digest "batches"/"coalesces" — a Truthful-UI/docs violation. Note: digest _rendering_ as a per-envelope compact form does work and is usable via subscription mode; only the coalescing + honest cost half is missing.
39	- Suggested fix: Either implement queue coalescing driven by `DigestFlushInterval`/`DigestMaxEnvelopes` (render one prompt from up to N envelopes and split prompt cost across them by canonical body size), or truthfully descope: drop the two dead config keys, remove the "batches/coalesces/summarized into one prompt" claims from web/docs/skill, and keep digest as the compact per-envelope mode it actually is.
40	
41	## B-004 — capability_match no-match path full-injects to top-K instead of digest fallback
42	
43	- File: internal/network/router.go
44	- Line: 1234
45	- Issue: When no peer's capability terms overlap the message, `activationScore` returns 0 for every peer (router.go:1290-1348), but `selectActivatedThreadPeers` still fills up to `activationTopK` peers by score-desc/PeerID-asc order and returns them as normal deliveries with empty `Mode`, which `applyDeliverySubscriptions` forces to `full` (manager.go:1155). There is no score threshold that drops zero-score peers and no downgrade to digest. `router_test.go:436` ("Should activate channel peers when no thread participants exist") asserts a full delivery to the sole channel peer with no capability match — i.e. the test encodes the divergent behavior.
46	- Rationale: Directly contradicts the spec's explicit rule: "If no match → digest fallback to thread/channel members — NEVER silently nothing, NEVER all-members full injection." The current behavior is bounded to K (default 3) but is still full injection to irrelevant peers with no digest downgrade, defeating the round's token-cost goal on exactly the unaddressed-thread case the round targets.
47	- Suggested fix: When the matcher yields no positive-score peer, emit the fallback deliveries with `Mode = digest` (to thread/channel members) rather than `full`, and record the observable activation reason. Update router_test.go:436 to assert digest fallback, not full injection.
48	
49	## B-005 — `mute` suppresses directly-addressed traffic (silent message loss)
50	
51	- File: internal/network/manager.go
52	- Line: 1179
53	- Issue: `deliverySubscriptionMode` (manager.go:1179-1239) exempts only mentioned peers (`deliveryMentionsPeer` → `Full` at 1187-1189). It has no exemption for addressed/directed (`To`) traffic. Directed messages reach `applyDeliverySubscriptions` on the inbound path (manager.go:1134); a direct-surface delivery is filtered to exactly the `To` peer via `localPeerMatchesConversation` (router.go), then `deliverySubscriptionMode` consults the channel-level subscription. If that peer has a `mute` row for the channel and is not mentioned, the mode resolves to `mute` and `applyDeliverySubscriptions` drops the delivery (manager.go:1161-1162).
54	- Rationale: Violates the explicit spec/plan invariant "mute suppresses only unmentioned/**unaddressed**" and the plan's "mute suppresses only unmentioned/unaddressed traffic." The failure is silent message loss: a peer who muted a channel will never receive a 1:1 direct message addressed to them. Addressed traffic must always be delivered.
55	- Suggested fix: Add an addressed exemption alongside the mention exemption, e.g. `if delivery.Envelope.IsDirected() && strings.TrimSpace(*delivery.Envelope.To) == delivery.PeerID { return store.NetworkSubscriptionModeFull, nil }`, and add a test asserting a muted peer still receives directed/direct messages.
56	
57	## B-006 — Entire subscription/mute/digest/keyword + activation-fallback delivery machinery ships with zero behavioral tests
58	
59	- File: internal/network/manager_test.go
60	- Line: null
61	- Issue: No test in `internal/network/*_test.go` references `deliverySubscriptionMode`, `firstApplicableSubscription`, `formatNetworkDigestMessage`, `applyDeliverySubscriptions`, `ListNetworkSubscriptions`, `selectActivatedThreadPeers`, `rankActivationCandidates`, or `activationScore` (confirmed by grep). The only new activation tests (router_test.go:436,501) assert the full-injection behavior from B-004. There is no coverage for subscription mode precedence (thread row wins over channel), empty-vs-non-empty keyword filters, mute-suppresses-only-unmentioned/unaddressed, digest rendering, or activation top-K ordering. Combined with the missing N≥2 fan-out test (B-002) and the missing status+body handler tests (see R-005), the round's new behaviors are largely unverified.
62	- Rationale: Violates the plan's own Test Plan (D7: "delivery tests for … durable guidance across reconnect/dropSession, digest coalescing, and honest cost allocation"; "router tests for … subscription precedence") and `agh-test-conventions`. This absence is the proximate cause of B-001…B-005 shipping broken — the invariants are unowned. Per project rule, tests exist to discover bugs; here they would have.
63	- Suggested fix: Extend the canonical suites (router_test, delivery_test, manager_test) with `t.Run("Should …")` subtests covering subscription precedence, keyword match/miss, mute-exempts-addressed/mentioned, digest fallback on no-match, and (once implemented) digest coalescing + honest cost split. No new standalone files — these invariants belong to the existing network suites.
64	
65	# Risks
66	
67	## R-001 — `delivery_structured_body_max_bytes` cap is unenforced (dead knob)
68	
69	- File: internal/network/delivery.go
70	- Line: 1137
71	- Issue: `formatNetworkMessageWithDeliveryMode` base64-encodes the full canonical body (`encodedBody = base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(deliveryBody.canonicalBody)`) with no truncation. `DeliveryStructuredBodyMaxBytes` (default 4096) is defined and validated (config.go:471,1757) and surfaced in settings, but never read in `internal/network`. The plan's "structured non-say bodies remain base64 JSON but are capped by network.delivery_structured_body_max_bytes" is not implemented.
72	- Suggested fix: Enforce the cap on the base64-encoded structured body (with a truncation marker + observability path for canonical bytes, which audit already stores), or delete the config key if the cap is not intended.
73	
74	## R-002 — Durable guidance store read is held under the delivery coordinator mutex (lock-during-IO)
75	
76	- File: internal/network/delivery.go
77	- Line: 514
78	- Issue: `guidanceModeForDelivery` holds `c.mu.Lock()` while calling `c.guidanceStore.GetNetworkDeliveryGuidanceState` — a synchronous SQLite `QueryRowContext`. The same `c.mu` guards accept/enqueue/`notifyWaiters`/`dropSession`/stats across every session on the daemon. On the first delivery per session (cold cache) a slow/contended global-DB read blocks all inbound accept/enqueue and stats. Bounded (once per session) but a real contention hazard under load.
79	- Suggested fix: Read the durable guidance state outside the lock, then re-acquire `c.mu` only to memoize the result.
80	
81	## R-003 — Fan-out partial failure leaves orphaned sibling runs (no rollback)
82	
83	- File: internal/api/core/tasks.go
84	- Line: 1213
85	- Issue: `enqueueFanOutTaskRuns` returns on the first `EnqueueRun` error with already-enqueued sibling runs left persisted, and the handler returns 500. A caller retry re-enqueues (per-designation idempotency keys mean prior successes may re-create under different keys). Result: live orphan runs sharing a `designation_group_id` with no rollup. (Moot until B-002 is fixed, but relevant afterward.)
86	- Suggested fix: Enqueue the group atomically (single tx) or define + document partial-fan-out semantics and return the partial set with the group id so callers can reconcile.
87	
88	## R-004 — Status-back per-sibling flooding + rollup completion lacks persistent transition de-dupe
89	
90	- File: internal/daemon/network_task_status_observer.go
91	- Line: 179
92	- Issue: For an N-sibling fan-out, each sibling's run_started/run_completed/run_failed posts a separate status message into the originating thread plus the final aggregate — noisier than the spec's "ONE compact message on meaningful transitions." Separately, `recomputeAndSendDesignationRollup` (232-258) sends the completion message from recomputed state and overwrites the persisted rollup without checking whether the previously-persisted rollup was already `Complete`; any future event replay/reconciliation that re-delivers a terminal event for a fully-terminal group re-sends the completion message. The happy path fires once (single-worker queue serializes), so this is latent.
93	- Suggested fix: Suppress per-run status posts when `run.DesignationGroupID != ""` (rely on the rollup); gate the completion send on a transition (previously-persisted rollup `Complete == false`), mirroring `bridgeTerminalTaskNotificationObserver`'s de-dupe.
94	
95	## R-005 — New API handlers have no status+body behavioral tests
96	
97	- File: internal/api/core/tasks.go
98	- Line: 1160
99	- Issue: `internal/api/core` has no subtests exercising `UpdateNetworkChannel`, `NetworkSubscriptions`/`UpsertNetworkSubscription`/`DeleteNetworkSubscription`, `PromoteNetworkThreadTask`, or `FanOutTaskRuns`. Coverage is limited to route-registration parity tables. Per `agh-test-conventions`, new agent-facing endpoints need assertions on status code AND body (e.g. fanout_policy normalization/validation error, the promote 201 body with `origin`, the fan-out 201 body with `designation_group_id`).
100	- Suggested fix: Add behavioral subtests to the existing `TestBaseHandlersNetworkEndpoints` and task surface suites asserting status + body for each new endpoint (including validation failures).
101	
102	## R-006 — Subscribing to a channel with no persisted `network_channels` row fails with an opaque FK error
103	
104	- File: internal/daemon/native_tools.go
105	- Line: 1776
106	- Issue: `networkSetSubscription` calls `PutNetworkSubscription` directly; the `network_subscriptions` FK to `network_channels(workspace_id, channel)` (global_db.go:174) is enforced, so subscribing/muting a channel that exists only as ephemeral traffic (or a typo, or not-yet-created channel) fails with a generic `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` surfaced as an opaque native error. No test covers the missing-channel path.
107	- Suggested fix: Verify/upsert the channel first and return a typed `ErrNetworkChannelNotFound` (mapped to a clean 404/validation error), and add a subscribe-before-channel-exists test.
108	
109	# Nits
110	
111	## N-001 — Router `activationTopK` hardcoded fallback (8) disagrees with config default (3)
112	
113	- File: internal/network/router.go
114	- Line: 219
115	- Issue: `newRouter` defaults `activationTopK` to 8 (router.go:219,234) while config default is 3 and docs state 3; only reachable if `WithRouterActivationTopK` is not called (production wires cfg=3), but confusing.
116	- Suggested fix: Align the fallback with the config default or drop the literal fallback.
117	
118	## N-002 — Raw-byte truncation of promotion digest / status text can split a UTF-8 rune
119	
120	- File: internal/daemon/native_tools.go
121	- Line: 3022
122	- Issue: `digest[:4000]` (native_tools.go) and `truncateStatusText` (network_task_status_observer.go:396) cut on byte boundaries, producing invalid UTF-8 mid-rune. `internal/situation/task_context.go:700` already has `truncateUTF8Bytes`.
123	- Suggested fix: Use rune-safe truncation for the pinned digest and status text.
124	
125	## N-003 — `NetworkConversationMessagePayloadFromStore` drops enrichment fields populated by the view converter
126	
127	- File: internal/api/core/network_conversations.go
128	- Line: 938
129	- Issue: The `FromStore` converter leaves `DisplayName`, `Local`, and presence fields unset, whereas `NetworkConversationMessagePayloadFromView` populates them; thread/direct timelines will report empty `display_name`/`local=false`.
130	- Suggested fix: Populate the enrichment fields in `FromStore` or confirm the thread/direct UI does not depend on them.
131	
132	## N-004 — `PromoteNetworkThreadTask` can leave an orphaned task if the origin-link write fails
133	
134	- File: internal/api/core/network_conversations.go
135	- Line: 143
136	- Issue: The task is created via `CreateTask`, then `writePromotedNetworkThreadOrigin`; if the origin write fails the handler returns 500 but the created task is not removed, leaving a task with no thread-origin link (inconsistent with the paired `Task`+`Origin` response contract).
137	- Suggested fix: Wrap create + origin write so a failed origin write rolls back the task, or document the create-only-on-partial-failure semantics.
138	
139	## N-005 — `task_designation_rollups` is currently write-only (no production reader)
140	
141	- File: internal/store/globaldb/global_db_network_preferences.go
142	- Line: 344
143	- Issue: `ListTaskDesignationRollups` has no non-test caller; the rollup is written (FanOutTaskRuns, status observer) but never read back, so the "read rollup" half is unexercised end-to-end.
144	- Suggested fix: Wire the rollup reader into the status-back/thread projection or confirm it is intentionally deferred.
145	
146	## N-006 — `networkResponseRegisterPromptSectionProvider.PromptSection` fallback returns the register unconditionally
147	
148	- File: internal/daemon/network_response_register_prompt.go
149	- Line: 31
150	- Issue: The bare `PromptSection` interface method returns the register with an empty channel regardless of predicate; not reached in production (ComposedAssembler prefers the startup-section path and the descriptor predicate gates emission), but a latent footgun if a future caller uses the bare seam.
151	- Suggested fix: Add a short comment documenting the method is a non-selecting interface stub, or return empty from it.
152	
153	# Evidence
154	
155	Read in full: the packet (`.compozy/tasks/network-token-optimization/codex-megaround-packet.txt`) and plan (`.codex/plans/20260701T200023-0300*…megaround.md`); root `CLAUDE.md` and `internal/CLAUDE.md`.
156	
157	First-hand verification by me (grep + targeted reads):
158	
159	- internal/network/router.go:1207-1348 (delivery-set computation, activation, no policy branch), :1362-1418 (directed routing, `localPeerMatchesConversation`).
160	- internal/network/manager.go:1090-1239 (inbound path, `applyDeliverySubscriptions`, `deliverySubscriptionMode` — mention-only exemption).
161	- internal/network/delivery.go:505-545 (guidance under mutex), :1122-1204 (structured base64 uncapped, single-envelope digest formatter).
162	- internal/store/globaldb/global_db_task_aux.go:735-775, 1477-1504 (designation-blind open-run guard) and internal/api/core/tasks.go:1195-1240 (`enqueueFanOutTaskRuns` sequential EnqueueRun).
163	- Config wiring greps confirming `DigestFlushInterval`/`DigestMaxEnvelopes`/`DeliveryStructuredBodyMaxBytes` are defined+validated but unread in `internal/network`; `fanout_policy`/`coordinator_peer_id` present across store/CLI/native/API/contract but absent from routing.
164	- Test-coverage grep confirming no `internal/network/*_test.go` references the subscription/mute/digest/activation functions; migration registry tail v44–v47 at global_db.go:1168-1186.
165	
166	Corroborating review-agent passes (read-only, evidence cross-checked against the above): persistence/migrations slice (append-only, workspace-scoped, BEGIN IMMEDIATE, no swallowed errors — clean); network delivery slice; task/fan-out slice (confirmed no parallel queue, `ClaimNextRun` authoritative, `agh.runtime` no impersonation, N ceiling range-validated); API/contract slice (parity matrix PASS, codegen co-ship PASS across openapi/agh.json + web/src/generated/agh-openapi.d.ts + sdk contracts); daemon prompt/register slice (response register wired, budget-enforced, guidance-only — clean); web+docs slice (confirmed the truthful-UI/docs violations for coordinator/all_members routing and digest coalescing, and that the round-1 zero-delivery path was cleanly deleted).
167	
168	Limitations: I did not run `make verify`, `make codegen-check`, or the test suites (read-only review; the diff is the working-tree state under commit `669f6b503 savepoint`). Findings are static-analysis + cross-referenced reads; B-001, B-002, B-003, B-005, and B-006 were verified by direct source reads, not merely subagent report.
169	
170	# Deferred Or Follow-Up
171	
172	- Confirm whether digest coalescing (B-003) is in scope for this round or deferred; if deferred, do the truthful descope (drop dead config keys + fix web/docs/skill copy) rather than leaving aspirational surfaces.
173	- After B-002 fix, add an integration test enqueuing N=2..5 designated runs through the real store and asserting group rollup fires once at quiescence.
174	- Re-review round is required after remediation given the blocker count and the "surfaces complete, behavior absent" pattern; do not treat green surfaces/parity as done until the delivery-plane and execution-plane behaviors are tested end-to-end.
175	- Backend note (out of this diff's fault): `networkChannelEntry` lookup at global_db_task_claim.go:935 filters by `channel` only (not workspace_id); pre-existing, guarded downstream, but worth closing when next touched.

1	AGH NETWORK MEGA-ROUND — CONVERSATION-PLANE EFFICIENCY + TWO-PLANES BRIDGE + DESIGNATED EXECUTION
2	==================================================================================================
3	
4	ROLE: You are the principal engineer for AGH, working in Plan Mode with gpt-5.5 xhigh reasoning. This is a
5	large, long-running redesign round — exactly what Plan Mode and your model tier exist for. Investigate
6	first (the required reading below is dense and load-bearing), then present ONE implementation plan that
7	sequences the full scope into ordered, independently verifiable phases. After approval you implement
8	hands-off until completion.
9	
10	This round builds ON TOP of the already-landed Round 1 (thread-membership routing + prompt-cost
11	accounting — committed on main; plan at .claude/plans/2026-07-01-network-thread-routing-cost-round1.md).
12	Round 1 is a prerequisite, not a draft: do not revert or re-litigate it. Where this round intentionally
13	REVERSES one Round 1 default (see D1 below), it does so as an explicit, documented hard cut.
14	
15	--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
16	PRODUCT FRAME (decided by the operator — these are constraints, not options)
17	--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
18	
19	AGH separates two planes:
20	
21	- CONVERSATION PLANE (network channels/threads): collaborative and cheap. Threads exist for deciding,
22	  reviewing, analyzing, planning, and discussing. Agents respond in a short, conversational register.
23	  Read-only lookups to answer a question are fine; heavy or mutating execution is NOT done in threads.
24	- EXECUTION PLANE (kanban tasks + autonomy kernel): owns real work. When a thread conversation produces
25	  actionable work, it is PROMOTED into a kanban task carrying a compact digest + pointer back to the
26	  thread. The kernel orchestrates execution — including fanning one task into N sub-runs of the SAME
27	  agent definition with DIFFERENT designation briefs — and compact status flows back into the
28	  originating thread as conversation.
29	
30	The bridge between the planes is first-class and agent-manageable. The golden register rule that must
31	reach agents through guidance: "threads are for deciding and discussing — reply short and conversational;
32	when actionable work emerges, promote it to a task and link the card; do not execute inside the thread."
33	
34	--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
35	REQUIRED READING (in this order, before planning; all paths repo-relative)
36	--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
37	
38	1. .compozy/tasks/network-token-optimization/analysis/summary.md — synthesized diagnosis, convergences,
39	   risks, the Round 1/Round 2 split record, and step 7 (response-register).
40	2. .claude/plans/2026-07-01-network-thread-routing-cost-round1.md — what Round 1 shipped (thread
41	   participants as routing boundary; zero-delivery default for unaddressed threads; PromptNetworkMeta
42	   prompt_size_bytes/estimated_prompt_tokens; migration v43 network_thread_peer_token_stats; cost payloads).
43	3. .compozy/tasks/network-token-optimization/analysis/08_analysis_channel-policy-surfaces.md — the
44	   implementation map for the conversation plane: fanout_policy storage (v44), activation hook at
45	   router.go deliveriesFromLocalPeers, deterministic capability matcher, mentions blast radius,
46	   volume verbs + network_subscriptions (v45), digest-fallback delivery mode, web surfaces.
47	4. .compozy/tasks/network-token-optimization/analysis/07_analysis_task-execution-plane.md — the
48	   implementation map for the bridge + execution plane: CreateTaskFromPeer (ZERO non-test callers today),
49	   withNetworkRunMetadata precedent, designation-brief seam (TaskRunPromptOverlay → opts.PromptOverlay →
50	   manager_start.go:369), fan-out ownership (EnqueueRun N times / coordinator_runtime.OnTaskRunEnqueued),
51	   per-run budgets (missing), artifact aggregation (priorRunSummaries precedent), status-back seam
52	   (composeTaskEventObserver + bridgeTerminalTaskNotificationObserver precedent), daemon-originated Send gap.
53	5. .compozy/tasks/network-token-optimization/analysis/06_analysis_response-behavior.md — why agents
54	   answer every thread message like a final report: no register guidance at any layer; the exact seams

1	# AGH Network Token Optimization Megaround
2	
3	## Summary
4	
5	Implement the packet as a hard-cut redesign that separates the conversation plane from the execution plane:
6	
7	- Conversation threads decide, discuss, review, and promote work; they do not execute heavy or mutating work directly.
8	- Actionable thread work is promoted into kanban tasks with typed origin links, compact digest context, and task/run status posted back to the source thread.
9	- Network deliveries become cheaper and more targeted through mention-aware routing, channel fanout policy, durable delivery guidance suppression, digest mode, subscriptions, and a short response register.
10	
11	No compatibility bridges or aliases will be added.
12	
13	## Implementation Changes
14	
15	### 1. Schema, Config, and Contracts
16	
17	- Append migrations after the current v43 tail:
18	  - v44: add `network_channels.fanout_policy`, `network_channels.coordinator_peer_id`, and `network_timeline_log.mentions_json`.
19	  - v45: add `network_subscriptions` keyed by `(workspace_id, channel, thread_id, peer_id)` plus `network_delivery_guidance_state` for durable per-session guidance suppression.
20	  - v46: add `network_task_thread_origins` keyed by `task_id`, with `workspace_id`, `channel`, `thread_id`, `origin_message_id`, compact digest, source message IDs, and timestamps.
21	  - v47: add `task_runs.designation_group_id`, an index on `(task_id, designation_group_id)`, and a small `task_designation_rollups` table keyed by designation group.
22	- Add config defaults:
23	  - `network.activation_top_k = 3`
24	  - `network.digest_flush_interval = 250ms`
25	  - `network.digest_max_envelopes = 10`
26	  - `network.response_guidance_max_bytes = 512`
27	  - `network.delivery_structured_body_max_bytes = 4096`
28	  - `task.orchestration.designated_run_max = 5`, validated in range `1..5`
29	- Extend public contracts and regenerate OpenAPI/types with `make codegen`:
30	  - `mentions []string` on network send requests, send payloads, envelopes, timeline messages, and prompt metadata.
31	  - `fanout_policy` and `coordinator_peer_id` on channel create/detail/update payloads.
32	  - subscription payloads with `mode: mute|digest|full` and optional `keyword_filters`.
33	  - task thread origin payloads and designated fan-out run payloads.
34	- Add or update HTTP/UDS surfaces:
35	  - `PATCH /api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/network/channels/{channel}` for fanout policy and coordinator.
36	  - channel/thread subscription list, set, and delete routes.
37	  - `POST /api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/network/channels/{channel}/threads/{thread_id}/promote`.
38	  - `POST /api/tasks/{task_id}/runs/fan-out`.
39	- Add or update native tools and CLI:
40	  - update `agh__network_send` and `agh network send` with repeatable `--mention`.
41	  - add channel update, subscribe, mute, unmute, and digest-mode tools/commands.
42	  - add `agh__task_promote_from_thread` and `agh task promote`.
43	  - add `agh__task_fanout_runs` and `agh task fan-out`.
44	
45	### 2. Conversation Plane Routing and Delivery Diet
46	
47	- Replace the current zero-delivery branch for unaddressed empty-participant threads with a deterministic activation resolver:
48	  - `capability_match` is the default channel policy.
49	  - `coordinator` routes to the configured `coordinator_peer_id`; missing or unavailable coordinator falls back to digest.
50	  - `all_members` is explicit opt-in and full-injects all eligible local peers.
51	- Capability matching is token-free and deterministic:
52	  - Use `SayBody.Intent` when present, otherwise `SayBody.Text`.
53	  - Score each local peer by normalized term overlap against capability ID and summary.
54	  - Select up to `network.activation_top_k` peers with positive scores, tie-breaking by peer ID.
55	  - If no peer matches, emit a digest fallback to eligible thread/channel subscribers and record an observable activation decision.
56	- Add mention semantics:
57	  - `Envelope.Mentions []string` is normalized, deduplicated, validated as peer IDs, cloned, logged, summarized, and rendered in prompt metadata/XML attrs.
58	  - Mention-only messages remain broadcast subjects; `subjectForEnvelope` stays direct only for `To`.
59	  - Mentioned peers receive full injection, become durable thread participants, and override fanout/digest defaults; `mute` suppresses only unmentioned/unaddressed traffic.
60	- Add subscription resolution at the delivery-set site:
61	  - Most-specific thread row wins over channel row.
62	  - Empty `keyword_filters` means always applicable.
63	  - Non-empty filters are lowercased substring guards over intent/text; if no filter matches, resolution falls through to the less-specific/default rule.
64	  - `mute` suppresses matching unmentioned traffic, `digest` converts matching full traffic to digest, and `full` preserves full injection.
65	- Add `DeliveryMode` with `full`, `queued`, and `digest`, plus activation/subscription reason fields for audit and hooks.
66	- Replace prompt bloat:
67	  - `say` bodies render as escaped plain text, not base64 JSON.
68	  - structured non-say bodies remain base64 JSON but are capped by `network.delivery_structured_body_max_bytes`.
69	  - protocol/reply guidance is suppressed through durable `network_delivery_guidance_state`, surviving reconnect and `dropSession`.
70	  - prompt metadata remains visible; if any adapter path cannot expose metadata, keep a compact in-band line rather than expanding guidance.
71	- Add digest formatting:
72	  - queue backlog and activation fallback can coalesce up to `network.digest_max_envelopes` into one digest prompt after `network.digest_flush_interval`.
73	  - prompt cost attribution is allocated across included envelopes by canonical envelope size, so totals match actual digest prompt cost instead of charging each envelope as if it received a full injection.
74	- Extend hook/audit payloads with activation reason, delivery mode, prompt size bytes, estimated tokens, digest envelope count, and subscription decision.
75	
76	### 3. Response Register and Execution Plane Bridge
77	
78	- Add a startup-gated, budget-capped network etiquette section through `ComposedAssembler`:
79	  - only active for network-capable sessions.
80	  - bounded by `network.response_guidance_max_bytes`.
81	  - states the golden rule: threads decide/discuss; actionable work is promoted to tasks; replies are short and only when addressed, activated, or adding value.
82	- Add a `TurnSourceNetwork` input augmenter:
83	  - one compact line before network prompts.
84	  - reinforces brevity, activation rules, and task promotion.
85	  - uses prompt metadata when available and falls back to compact channel/thread/message text only when required.
86	- Implement thread-to-task promotion:
87	  - create a compact pin-and-trim digest around the origin message using `task.orchestration.summary_max_bytes`.
88	  - store typed origin data in `network_task_thread_origins`.
89	  - create the task only; do not enqueue a run unless the caller separately uses an explicit enqueue/fan-out surface.
90	  - web thread detail shows a promote action and linked task card; task views link back to the source thread.
91	- Add status-back:
92	  - add a task event observer to `composeTaskEventObserver`.
93	  - for tasks with network thread origins, post one compact status message on meaningful lifecycle transitions and on designation rollup completion.
94	  - use a first-class runtime peer identity, `agh.runtime`, through a new runtime/system send path; do not impersonate a session peer.
95	- Implement designated sub-runs:
96	  - add `FanOutRuns` that validates `N <= task.orchestration.designated_run_max` and enqueues each run through authoritative `EnqueueRun`.
97	  - each run gets `designation_group_id` plus metadata containing index, count, brief, origin, and prompt budget.
98	  - render designation briefs through `TaskRunPromptOverlay -> opts.PromptOverlay -> manager_start.go`.
99	  - when all runs in a group are terminal, write a rollup artifact and emit one task status-back message to the originating thread.
100	
101	### 4. Web, Docs, Skills, and Cleanup
102	
103	- Update web network/thread surfaces to expose:
104	  - channel fanout policy and coordinator editing.
105	  - mentions in the composer.
106	  - subscription controls for mute, digest, and full.
107	  - thread promotion and linked task cards.
108	  - designated fan-out entry point from task surfaces.
109	- Keep UI token-compliant with `packages/ui/src/tokens.css` and `DESIGN.md`; no invented visual grammar.
110	- Update docs and agent guidance:
111	  - `packages/site` network, task, native-tool, and config docs.
112	  - `skills/agh/SKILL.md` and relevant references for mentions, subscriptions, task promotion, status-back, designated fan-out, and the two-plane golden rule.
113	  - `COPY.md` vocabulary remains authoritative; use “capability” terminology.
114	- Delete obsolete behavior instead of bridging:
115	  - remove silent zero-delivery for empty participant threads.
116	  - remove session-local-only protocol guidance suppression.
117	  - remove mandatory base64 JSON prompt rendering for chat `say` bodies.
118	  - remove single-envelope assumptions in delivery prompts where digest mode applies.
119	- Keep all changes workspace-scoped where network data crosses workspaces; every new store query and API route must include `workspace_id`.
120	
121	## Test Plan
122	
123	- Test placement decisions before writing tests:
124	  - Routing/mentions/subscriptions invariant: owning layer `internal/network`; canonical suite existing router/delivery tests.
125	  - Schema/storage invariant: owning layer `internal/store/globaldb`; canonical migration/store suites.
126	  - API/UDS/native/CLI parity invariant: owning layers `internal/api`, `internal/daemon`, and CLI suites.
127	  - Task promotion/status-back/fan-out invariant: owning layers `internal/task` and `internal/daemon`; use existing task manager and observer suites.
128	  - Web behavior invariant: existing web system/component tests only where runtime behavior is user-visible; no snapshot or config-existence filler tests.
129	- Focused checks during implementation:
130	  - migration fresh DB and reopen tests for v44-v47.
131	  - router tests for `capability_match`, `coordinator`, `all_members`, no-match digest fallback, mentions, `To` precedence, and subscription precedence.
132	  - delivery tests for plain-text `say`, structured body cap, durable guidance across reconnect/dropSession, digest coalescing, and honest cost allocation.
133	  - task tests for promotion origin storage, no auto-enqueue, status-back observer, runtime peer identity, fan-out validation, overlay rendering, and group rollup.
134	  - contract/API/CLI/native tests for all new public surfaces.
135	  - web tests for mentions, subscription controls, promotion links, and fan-out affordance.
136	- Required final verification:
137	  - `make codegen`
138	  - `make codegen-check`
139	  - focused Go and Bun/Turbo tests for changed packages.
140	  - `agh-ui-screenshot` captures for changed network/task UI stories or routes.
141	  - `make verify` passing with zero warnings/errors.
142	
143	## Assumptions and Defaults
144	
145	- `fanout_policy = capability_match` is the default for all new and existing channels after the hard-cut migration.
146	- `coordinator_peer_id` is explicit per channel; no naming convention or implicit “coordinator” capability is used.
147	- Mentions are explicit activation and full-injection signals; they do not change broadcast subject routing.
148	- Explicit `To` keeps existing directed semantics and remains stronger than mention/fanout policy.

33			) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)

561	func normalizeStringSlice(values []string) []string {
562		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(values))
563		normalized := make([]string, 0, len(values))
564		for _, value := range values {
565			trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(value)
566			if trimmed == "" {
567				continue
568			}
569			if _, ok := seen[trimmed]; ok {
570				continue
571			}
572			seen[trimmed] = struct{}{}
573			normalized = append(normalized, trimmed)
574		}
575		return normalized
576	}

130	func newDaemonNativeProvider(deps *daemonNativeToolsDeps) (toolspkg.Provider, error) {
131		if deps == nil {
132			return nil, errors.New("daemon: native tool dependencies are required")
133		}
134		adapter := &daemonNativeTools{deps: deps}
135		bindings := adapter.bindings()
136		descriptors := builtintools.NativeDescriptors()
137		nativeTools := make([]toolspkg.NativeTool, 0, len(descriptors))
138		for _, descriptor := range descriptors {
139			binding, ok := bindings[descriptor.ID]
140			if !ok {
141				return nil, fmt.Errorf("daemon: missing native handler for %s", descriptor.ID)
142			}
143			nativeTools = append(nativeTools, toolspkg.NativeTool{
144				Descriptor:   descriptor,
145				Call:         binding.call,
146				Availability: binding.availability,
147			})
148		}
149		return toolspkg.NewNativeProvider(builtintools.Source(), nativeTools...)
150	}

152	func (d *Daemon) bootToolRegistry(_ context.Context, state *bootState) error {
153		if state == nil {
154			return errors.New("daemon: tool registry state is required")
155		}
156		if state.mcpServerCatalog == nil {
157			state.mcpServerCatalog = newResourceCatalog(cloneDaemonMCPServer)
158		}
159		var registry *toolspkg.RuntimeRegistry
160		var mcpAuth toolspkg.MCPAuthStatusProvider
161		deps := d.nativeToolsDeps(state, func() toolspkg.Registry {
162			return registry
163		})
164		deps.MCPAuth = func() toolspkg.MCPAuthStatusProvider {
165			return mcpAuth
166		}
167		provider, err := newDaemonNativeProvider(&deps)
168		if err != nil {
169			return fmt.Errorf("daemon: create native tool provider: %w", err)
170		}
171		approvalTokens := toolspkg.NewApprovalTokenStore(state.cfg.Tools.Policy.ApprovalTimeout())
172		var approvalBridge *toolApprovalBridge
173		if _, ok := state.sessions.(sessionPermissionRequester); ok {
174			approvalBridge = newToolApprovalBridge(
175				func() sessionPermissionRequester {
176					requester, ok := state.sessions.(sessionPermissionRequester)
177					if !ok {
178						return nil
179					}
180					return requester
181				},
182				state.cfg.Tools.Policy.ApprovalTimeout(),
183				approvalTokens,
184			)
185		} else {
186			approvalBridge = newToolApprovalBridge(nil, state.cfg.Tools.Policy.ApprovalTimeout(), approvalTokens)
187		}
188		toolsets, err := builtintools.ToolsetCatalog()
189		if err != nil {
190			return fmt.Errorf("daemon: build native toolset catalog: %w", err)
191		}
192		policyResolver, err := newNativeToolPolicyResolverForBoot(state)
193		if err != nil {
194			return fmt.Errorf("daemon: build native tool policy resolver: %w", err)
195		}
196		providers := []toolspkg.Provider{provider}
197		extensionProvider, err := newDaemonExtensionToolProvider(state)
198		if err != nil {
199			return fmt.Errorf("daemon: create extension tool provider: %w", err)
200		}
201		if extensionProvider != nil {
202			providers = append(providers, extensionProvider)
203		}
204		mcpProvider, mcpAuthProvider, err := d.newDaemonMCPToolProvider(state)
205		if err != nil {
206			return fmt.Errorf("daemon: create mcp tool provider: %w", err)
207		}
208		mcpAuth = mcpAuthProvider
209		if mcpProvider != nil {
210			providers = append(providers, mcpProvider)
211		}
212		registryOptions := []toolspkg.RegistryOption{
213			toolspkg.WithProviders(providers...),
214			toolspkg.WithPolicyInputResolver(policyResolver, toolsets),
215			toolspkg.WithApprovalBridge(approvalBridge),
216			toolspkg.WithDefaultMaxResultBytes(state.cfg.Tools.DefaultMaxResultBytes),
217		}
218		registryOptions = appendToolEventSinkOption(registryOptions, state.registry, d.now)
219		registry, err = toolspkg.NewRegistry(registryOptions...)
220		if err != nil {
221			return fmt.Errorf("daemon: create tool registry: %w", err)
222		}
223		state.toolRegistry = registry
224		state.toolsets = registry
225		state.toolApprovals = approvalTokens
226		state.deps.ToolRegistry = registry
227		state.deps.Toolsets = registry
228		state.deps.ToolApprovals = approvalTokens
229		return nil
230	}

324			}),
325			executor,

358	func daemonMCPServerConfigs(state *bootState) []aghconfig.MCPServer {
359		if state == nil {
360			return nil
361		}
362		servers := make([]aghconfig.MCPServer, 0, len(state.cfg.MCPServers))
363		seen := map[string]struct{}{}
364		add := func(server aghconfig.MCPServer) {
365			name := strings.TrimSpace(server.Name)
366			if name == "" {
367				return
368			}
369			if _, ok := seen[name]; ok {
370				return
371			}
372			seen[name] = struct{}{}
373			servers = append(servers, cloneDaemonMCPServer(server))
374		}
375		for _, server := range state.cfg.MCPServers {
376			add(server)
377		}
378		providerNames := make([]string, 0, len(state.cfg.Providers))
379		for name := range state.cfg.Providers {
380			providerNames = append(providerNames, name)
381		}
382		slices.Sort(providerNames)
383		for _, name := range providerNames {
384			for _, server := range state.cfg.Providers[name].MCPServers {
385				add(server)
386			}
387		}
388		if state.mcpServerCatalog != nil {
389			for _, record := range state.mcpServerCatalog.Snapshot() {
390				add(record.Spec)
391			}
392		}
393		return servers
394	}

396	func daemonMCPSources(state *bootState) []toolspkg.SourceRef {
397		if state == nil {
398			return nil
399		}
400		sources := make([]toolspkg.SourceRef, 0, len(state.cfg.MCPServers))
401		seen := map[string]struct{}{}
402		add := func(server aghconfig.MCPServer, source toolspkg.SourceRef) {
403			name := strings.TrimSpace(server.Name)
404			if name == "" {
405				return
406			}
407			if _, ok := seen[name]; ok {
408				return
409			}
410			seen[name] = struct{}{}
411			source.Kind = toolspkg.SourceMCP
412			source.Owner = name
413			source.RawServerName = name
414			sources = append(sources, source)
415		}
416		for _, server := range state.cfg.MCPServers {
417			add(server, toolspkg.SourceRef{})
418		}
419		providerNames := make([]string, 0, len(state.cfg.Providers))
420		for name := range state.cfg.Providers {
421			providerNames = append(providerNames, name)
422		}
423		slices.Sort(providerNames)
424		for _, name := range providerNames {
425			for _, server := range state.cfg.Providers[name].MCPServers {
426				add(server, toolspkg.SourceRef{})
427			}
428		}
429		if state.mcpServerCatalog != nil {
430			for _, record := range state.mcpServerCatalog.Snapshot() {
431				add(record.Spec, toolspkg.SourceRef{
432					ResourceID:      record.ID,
433					ResourceVersion: fmt.Sprint(record.Version),
434					WorkspaceID:     record.Scope.ID,
435					Scope:           string(record.Scope.Kind),
436				})
437			}
438		}
439		return sources
440	}

313	func (o *networkTaskStatusObserver) designationRollup(
314		ctx context.Context,
315		event taskpkg.Event,
316		run taskpkg.Run,
317	) (taskDesignationRollupStatus, error) {
318		groupID := strings.TrimSpace(run.DesignationGroupID)
319		runs, err := o.tasks.ListTaskRuns(ctx, taskpkg.RunQuery{
320			TaskID:             strings.TrimSpace(run.TaskID),
321			DesignationGroupID: groupID,
322		})
323		if err != nil {
324			return taskDesignationRollupStatus{}, fmt.Errorf("list designated task runs: %w", err)
325		}
326		rollup := taskDesignationRollupStatus{
327			DesignationGroupID: groupID,
328			TaskID:             strings.TrimSpace(run.TaskID),
329			RunIDs:             make([]string, 0, len(runs)),
330			Statuses:           make(map[string]int),
331			UpdatedAt:          o.now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano),
332			LatestEvent:        strings.TrimSpace(event.EventType),
333			LatestEventID:      strings.TrimSpace(event.ID),
334		}
335		for _, item := range runs {
336			runID := strings.TrimSpace(item.ID)
337			if runID != "" {
338				rollup.RunIDs = append(rollup.RunIDs, runID)
339			}
340			status := item.Status.Normalize()
341			statusKey := string(status)
342			rollup.Statuses[statusKey]++
343			switch status {
344			case taskpkg.TaskRunStatusCompleted:
345				rollup.Completed++
346				rollup.TerminalCount++
347			case taskpkg.TaskRunStatusFailed:
348				rollup.Failed++
349				rollup.TerminalCount++
350			case taskpkg.TaskRunStatusCanceled:
351				rollup.Canceled++
352				rollup.TerminalCount++
353			case taskpkg.TaskRunStatusQueued:
354				rollup.Queued++
355			case taskpkg.TaskRunStatusNeedsAttention:
356				rollup.NeedsAttention++
357			default:
358				rollup.Running++
359			}
360		}
361		slices.Sort(rollup.RunIDs)
362		rollup.Total = len(rollup.RunIDs)
363		rollup.Complete = rollup.Total > 0 && rollup.TerminalCount == rollup.Total
364		return rollup, nil
365	}

# Summary

All six round-1 blockers (B-001..B-006) are remediated at the code level and, critically, are now
owned by behavioral tests — channel fanout policy is enforced in routing with coordinator/all_members/
capability_match branches, designated fan-out N≥2 works through the real store, digest mode coalesces
with honest per-envelope cost allocation, capability no-match downgrades to digest fallback, mute
exempts addressed traffic, and the subscription/mute/digest/activation machinery has real assertions.
Every round-1 risk except R-003 (partial fan-out orphans, now live because B-002 was fixed) is resolved,
generated artifacts co-ship correctly across openapi/web/sdk, CLI/HTTP/UDS/native parity is complete,
and no new blocker was found — the residual items are non-blocking risks and nits.

# Blockers

None.

# Risks

## R-201 — Partial fan-out failure leaves orphaned sibling runs (round-1 R-003, now live)

- File: internal/api/core/tasks.go
- Line: 1213
- Issue: `enqueueFanOutTaskRuns` (tasks.go:1213-1240) loops `manager.EnqueueRun` once per designation and returns on the first error, leaving already-enqueued siblings persisted as `queued` runs; the handler then returns 500 and `PutTaskDesignationRollup` is never written for that group (tasks.go:1185-1196). This was round-1 R-003, previously moot because B-002 made fan-out non-functional; now that B-002 is fixed and N≥2 works, the partial-failure path is reachable. The most likely trigger is a failure on designation ≥2 (transient DB error, per-designation metadata issue) after designation 1 already created a run. A client retry generates a fresh `groupID` (`store.NewID("tdg")`, tasks.go:1178) with per-index idempotency keys, so the orphan from the failed attempt is stranded under the old group while a new group is created. The observer self-heals partially (`recomputeAndSendDesignationRollup` recomputes from live runs), but the stray run still executes and posts status-back under an abandoned group.
- Suggested fix: Enqueue the designation group atomically (single tx spanning all `ReserveQueuedRun` calls), or on partial failure roll back the already-enqueued siblings; alternatively define and document partial-fan-out semantics and return the partial set + group id so callers can reconcile. Add a test asserting no orphan `queued` rows remain after a mid-group enqueue failure.

## R-202 — Rollup completion status-back can double-send under concurrent sibling termination

- File: internal/daemon/network_task_status_observer.go
- Line: 245
- Issue: `recomputeAndSendDesignationRollup` gates the completion message on a transition by reading the previously-persisted rollup via `previousDesignationRollupComplete` (observer.go:270-292), then persisting, then sending only when `!wasComplete && rollup.Complete`. The read-compute-persist-check-send sequence is not atomic. Sibling runs can execute in different sessions and terminate concurrently, firing two `run_completed` events into two observer invocations. If both read `wasComplete=false` before either persists, both compute `Complete=true` and both send, producing a duplicate `task_fanout_rollup` status-back into the thread. This is cosmetic noise (not data corruption) and low-probability (requires two siblings terminal within the observer window), but the dedup is best-effort rather than race-free.
- Suggested fix: Make the completion decision atomic — e.g. persist the rollup and detect the incomplete→complete transition inside a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` tx that returns whether this call was the one that flipped `Complete`, and send only on that signal; or serialize designation-group rollup handling per group id.

## R-203 — Positive-path activation and keyword-filter matches are untested

- File: internal/network/router_test.go
- Line: 436
- Issue: B-006 is substantially closed (11 of 13 delivery invariants now have `t.Run("Should …")` behavioral tests with real assertions), but two positive paths remain uncovered: (a) `capability_match` WITH a positive score — no test asserts that a matching peer is activated as `full` injection (only the no-match→digest-fallback path at router_test.go:436 is tested); (b) keyword filter WITH a match — only the miss case is tested (manager_test.go:1914 asserts digest fallback when the filter misses), so the "filter matches → deliver full" branch of `subscriptionKeywordFiltersMatch` (manager.go:1271-1286) is unexercised. Both are the "happy path" of features whose failure modes (over- or under-delivery) directly affect the round's token-cost goal.
- Suggested fix: Add two subtests to the canonical suites — one asserting a capability-matched peer receives `full` (Mode empty/full) when its catalog overlaps the intent terms, and one asserting a full-mode subscription with a matching keyword filter delivers `full`.

# Nits

## N-201 — Every digest delivery incurs the full flush-interval latency even for a single envelope

- File: internal/network/delivery.go
- Line: 688
- Issue: `collectDigestBatch` blocks the per-session delivery worker for the entire `digestFlushInterval` (default 250ms) whenever the head item is digest-mode and `digestMaxEnvelopes > 1`, even when no additional envelopes are waiting — adding a fixed 250ms latency to every digest delivery, not only coalesced ones.
- Suggested fix: Skip the flush wait when the queue holds no further digest-eligible items for the peer, or short-circuit the timer once the queue drains.

## N-202 — `task_designation_rollups` reader is used only by the dedup path

- File: internal/store/globaldb/global_db_network_preferences.go
- Line: 344
- Issue: `ListTaskDesignationRollups` now has exactly one non-test caller — the observer's `previousDesignationRollupComplete` dedup read — so the persisted rollup summary is never surfaced to an API/CLI/UDS/thread projection for agents or operators to read back the fan-out result.
- Suggested fix: Confirm the write-mostly rollup is intentional for this round, or wire a read surface (task detail / thread projection) so the aggregated designation result is observable.

All six round-1 blockers (B-001..B-006) are remediated at the code level and, critically, are now
owned by behavioral tests — channel fanout policy is enforced in routing with coordinator/all_members/
capability_match branches, designated fan-out N≥2 works through the real store, digest mode coalesces
with honest per-envelope cost allocation, capability no-match downgrades to digest fallback, mute
exempts addressed traffic, and the subscription/mute/digest/activation machinery has real assertions.
Every round-1 risk except R-003 (partial fan-out orphans, now live because B-002 was fixed) is resolved,
generated artifacts co-ship correctly across openapi/web/sdk, CLI/HTTP/UDS/native parity is complete,
and no new blocker was found — the residual items are non-blocking risks and nits.

# Blockers

None.

# Risks

## R-201 — Partial fan-out failure leaves orphaned sibling runs (round-1 R-003, now live)

- File: internal/api/core/tasks.go
- Line: 1213
- Issue: `enqueueFanOutTaskRuns` (tasks.go:1213-1240) loops `manager.EnqueueRun` once per designation and returns on the first error, leaving already-enqueued siblings persisted as `queued` runs; the handler then returns 500 and `PutTaskDesignationRollup` is never written for that group (tasks.go:1185-1196). This was round-1 R-003, previously moot because B-002 made fan-out non-functional; now that B-002 is fixed and N≥2 works, the partial-failure path is reachable. The most likely trigger is a failure on designation ≥2 (transient DB error, per-designation metadata issue) after designation 1 already created a run. A client retry generates a fresh `groupID` (`store.NewID("tdg")`, tasks.go:1178) with per-index idempotency keys, so the orphan from the failed attempt is stranded under the old group while a new group is created. The observer self-heals partially (`recomputeAndSendDesignationRollup` recomputes from live runs), but the stray run still executes and posts status-back under an abandoned group.
- Suggested fix: Enqueue the designation group atomically (single tx spanning all `ReserveQueuedRun` calls), or on partial failure roll back the already-enqueued siblings; alternatively define and document partial-fan-out semantics and return the partial set + group id so callers can reconcile. Add a test asserting no orphan `queued` rows remain after a mid-group enqueue failure.

## R-202 — Rollup completion status-back can double-send under concurrent sibling termination

- File: internal/daemon/network_task_status_observer.go
- Line: 245
- Issue: `recomputeAndSendDesignationRollup` gates the completion message on a transition by reading the previously-persisted rollup via `previousDesignationRollupComplete` (observer.go:270-292), then persisting, then sending only when `!wasComplete && rollup.Complete`. The read-compute-persist-check-send sequence is not atomic. Sibling runs can execute in different sessions and terminate concurrently, firing two `run_completed` events into two observer invocations. If both read `wasComplete=false` before either persists, both compute `Complete=true` and both send, producing a duplicate `task_fanout_rollup` status-back into the thread. This is cosmetic noise (not data corruption) and low-probability (requires two siblings terminal within the observer window), but the dedup is best-effort rather than race-free.
- Suggested fix: Make the completion decision atomic — e.g. persist the rollup and detect the incomplete→complete transition inside a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` tx that returns whether this call was the one that flipped `Complete`, and send only on that signal; or serialize designation-group rollup handling per group id.

## R-203 — Positive-path activation and keyword-filter matches are untested

- File: internal/network/router_test.go
- Line: 436
- Issue: B-006 is substantially closed (11 of 13 delivery invariants now have `t.Run("Should …")` behavioral tests with real assertions), but two positive paths remain uncovered: (a) `capability_match` WITH a positive score — no test asserts that a matching peer is activated as `full` injection (only the no-match→digest-fallback path at router_test.go:436 is tested); (b) keyword filter WITH a match — only the miss case is tested (manager_test.go:1914 asserts digest fallback when the filter misses), so the "filter matches → deliver full" branch of `subscriptionKeywordFiltersMatch` (manager.go:1271-1286) is unexercised. Both are the "happy path" of features whose failure modes (over- or under-delivery) directly affect the round's token-cost goal.
- Suggested fix: Add two subtests to the canonical suites — one asserting a capability-matched peer receives `full` (Mode empty/full) when its catalog overlaps the intent terms, and one asserting a full-mode subscription with a matching keyword filter delivers `full`.

# Nits

## N-201 — Every digest delivery incurs the full flush-interval latency even for a single envelope

- File: internal/network/delivery.go
- Line: 688
- Issue: `collectDigestBatch` blocks the per-session delivery worker for the entire `digestFlushInterval` (default 250ms) whenever the head item is digest-mode and `digestMaxEnvelopes > 1`, even when no additional envelopes are waiting — adding a fixed 250ms latency to every digest delivery, not only coalesced ones.
- Suggested fix: Skip the flush wait when the queue holds no further digest-eligible items for the peer, or short-circuit the timer once the queue drains.

## N-202 — `task_designation_rollups` reader is used only by the dedup path

- File: internal/store/globaldb/global_db_network_preferences.go
- Line: 344
- Issue: `ListTaskDesignationRollups` now has exactly one non-test caller — the observer's `previousDesignationRollupComplete` dedup read — so the persisted rollup summary is never surfaced to an API/CLI/UDS/thread projection for agents or operators to read back the fan-out result.
- Suggested fix: Confirm the write-mostly rollup is intentional for this round, or wire a read surface (task detail / thread projection) so the aggregated designation result is observable.
